title: Phase 0: Bootstrap
description: Solution skeleton, deterministic RNG and math, sampler, byte tokenizer, placeholder model, OpenAI-style API, MCP server, CI with golden hashes

title: Phase 1: Kernels
description: Tensor type, deterministic matmul with fixed tiling, RMSNorm, RoPE, SiLU/GELU, attention with fixed-order softmax

title: Phase 2: Import existing models
description: Llama-style decoder with KV cache; `dllm import` for small open-weight models (SmolLM2-135M first); BPE tokenizer and chat templates

title: Phase 3: Fine-tuning (optional)
description: Deterministic backprop and AdamW on imported weights, fixed data order, reproducible checkpoints

title: Phase 4: API parity
description: Streaming (SSE), tool calling, JSON-schema output, Anthropic Messages endpoint, embeddings

title: Phase 5: MCP, both directions
description: Richer MCP server (prompts, resources); MCP client host so the model can call external tools

title: Phase 6: Performance
description: SIMD and multi-threading with batch-invariant reduction order, integer quantisation, GPU kernels

title: Phase 7: Usability and releases
description: Pre-built wheels and tagged releases, PyPI, CUDA install route checked in CI, Docker image, web chat UI, a larger verified model

title: Phase 8: Serving and ecosystem
description: Prompt caching and batched concurrent decoding with each request's solo bits, Ollama-compatible API, OpenAI Responses API, Qwen3, LoRA adapters

title: Phase 9: Mainstream model families
description: SentencePiece-style tokenizers, Mistral and sliding-window attention, Gemma 2/3, Phi-3/Phi-4-mini, OLMo 2, Granite 3.x, a verified Llama 3.2

title: Phase 10: Portable determinism
description: Identical output across machines as a guarantee: canonical floating point environment, tokenizer and template independent of Python/regex/Jinja versions, real-model golden answers on every release platform, dllm verify

title: Phase 11: Interpretability and editing
description: Activation tracing, logit lens, embedding explorer and word clouds, attention maps, steering vectors, ROME model edits and sparse autoencoders, all bit-reproducible

title: Phase 12: Retrieval and grounding
description: Embedding models with last-token pooling and query prompts, an exact reproducible document index, chats grounded in it in every front end, an MCP search tool

title: Phase 13: Speed without changing a bit
description: Register-tiled float32 and Q8_0 matmuls, tiled prefill attention, parallel fused activations, a low-latency thread pool; every golden hash unchanged

title: Phase 14: Lean and fast decoding
description: Speculative decoding that changes no bit, Q4_0 weights with exact integer sums, one copy of the weights in memory

title: Phase 15: Verifiable outputs
description: Content-derived receipts for every response, dllm replay to verify them bit for bit, a prompt cache that survives restarts, reproducible evaluation

title: Phase 16: Reproducible agents
description: Agent transcripts of MCP tool loops, offline replay with recorded tool results, built-in deterministic tools, receipt chains for conversations

title: Phase 17: Verifiable models
description: Model lineage in every model file, training receipts that replay a fine-tune bit for bit, byte-identical model files on every platform, signed receipts and models

title: Phase 18: Deterministic serving at scale
description: An exact response cache, coalescing of identical in-flight requests, self-audits and dllm audit to check that servers give the same bits

title: Phase 19: Reproducible model building
description: Exact model merges recorded in the lineage, exports to safetensors and GGUF that import to the same weights, distillation that replays bit for bit

title: Phase 20: Independent verification
description: A pure-Python reference implementation that gives the C++ kernels' bits, dllm verify --reference, conformance vectors for other implementations, and a written determinism specification

title: Phase 21: Deterministic decoding controls
description: Repetition, frequency and presence penalties, min-p and logit bias with a fixed order; several choices per request with each its solo bits; regex-constrained output; all in the specification, the reference implementation and the conformance vectors

title: Phase 22: Reproducible batch jobs
description: dllm batch over OpenAI batch files with byte-identical output at any concurrency, exact resume after an interruption, the OpenAI Files and Batches API with content-derived ids, and one verifiable digest per batch

title: Phase 23: Long conversations in a fixed window
description: The model's context window enforced everywhere, deterministic truncation of long conversations, rolling context to generate past the window with exactly defined bits, all in the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 24: Reproducible reasoning
description: Thinking models done deterministically: the reasoning separated from the answer in every API, thinking switched on or off per request, and an exact thinking budget, all recorded in receipts and the specification

title: Phase 25: Reproducible preference tuning
description: Direct preference optimisation (DPO) on chosen/rejected pairs with the same bits on every machine: a fixed pair order, exact reference log-probabilities, checkpoints and training receipts that replay bit for bit, and a deterministic preference evaluation

title: Phase 26: Exact hybrid search and reranking
description: Exact lexical (BM25) search stored in the index, hybrid ranking with a fixed fusion rule, reranking with a language model and a /v1/rerank endpoint, all giving the same ranking on every machine

title: Phase 27: Verifiable text watermarks
description: Statistical watermarks in generated text with exactly defined bits: a keyed green-list bias in the sampler, exact detection from the text alone, the watermark in receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 28: Reproducible scoring and voting
description: The OpenAI completions API with exact prompt scoring (echo and logprobs), self-consistency voting over several sampled answers with a total order, and both in receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 29: Exact guided decoding
description: Decoding that combines several distributions with exactly defined bits: classifier-free guidance with a negative prompt, contrastive decoding against a smaller amateur model, and logit ensembles of models that share a tokenizer, all in receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 30: Exact beam search
description: Beam search with a total order on hypotheses, length penalties and n-best lists, so the best sequences by exact log-probability are the same on every machine, in receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 31: Exact JSON Schema constraints
description: Structured output that enforces string patterns and formats, string lengths and integer bounds exactly, compiled to byte automata, so every answer is valid under the full schema and the same on every machine

title: Phase 32: Exact context-free grammars
description: Constrained decoding with user-supplied GBNF grammars (rules, recursion, repetition, character classes) compiled to the byte pushdown automaton, in every API and the CLI, so grammar-shaped answers are exact and the same on every machine

title: Phase 33: Exact numeric and object constraints
description: Structured output that also enforces bounds on decimal numbers, multipleOf, property counts and typed map objects exactly, compiled to byte automata, so more schemas are enforced in full and the same on every machine

title: Phase 34: Exact tuples, key names and unique items
description: Structured output that enforces tuples (prefixItems), constrained property names (propertyNames) and uniqueItems over finite item sets exactly, so pydantic-style schemas are enforced in full and the same on every machine

title: Phase 35: Exact schema combinators
description: Structured output that enforces allOf, not, if/then/else, patternProperties and contains exactly, by merging and negating schemas before they are compiled to byte automata, so schemas built from combinators are enforced in full and the same on every machine

title: Phase 36: Exact token healing
description: Token healing with exactly defined bits: a prompt that ends inside a word is backed up by its last token and the answer is constrained to start with that token's bytes, for raw prompts and chat prefills, in every API, receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 37: Exact fill-in-the-middle
description: Fill-in-the-middle completions with exactly defined bits: a prompt and a suffix rendered with the model's own FIM tokens, the completions API suffix, Ollama's suffix and dllm generate --suffix, in receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 38: Exact length and stop controls
description: Length and stop controls with exactly defined bits: a minimum answer length, ignoring the end-of-sequence token, extra stop token ids and stop strings kept in the output, in the OpenAI APIs and the CLI, receipts, the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 39: Deterministic MCP sampling, prompts and resources
description: The MCP host completed: servers that ask the client to sample get exact answers from the engine, MCP prompts and resources feed conversations in a fixed order, all in dllm chat and the host API, with the same bits on every run

title: Phase 40: Reproducible fine-tuning of every model family
description: Fine-tuning, LoRA, DPO and distillation for every architecture the engine runs: OLMo 2, Granite, Gemma 2/3 and Phi-3/Phi-4-mini with LongRoPE, with fixed-order backward kernels for their norms, activations and soft-caps and the same gradient bits on every machine

title: Phase 41: Exact long-context RoPE scaling
description: Longer context windows with exactly defined bits: YaRN RoPE scaling from Hugging Face and GGUF models, dllm import --context-length to extend Qwen-style models with YaRN and Phi-3/Phi-4-mini to their full LongRoPE context, fixed per model file so every token uses the same frequencies, in the specification and the reference implementation

title: Phase 42: Exact mixture-of-experts models
description: Mixture-of-experts models with exactly defined bits: Qwen3-MoE, OLMoE and Mixtral routed with a fixed-order softmax and a total-order top-k, experts combined in a fixed order, batch-invariant on CPU and GPU, imported from Hugging Face and GGUF, in the specification, the reference implementation and the interpretability tools

title: Phase 43: Reproducible fine-tuning of mixture-of-experts models
description: Fine-tuning, LoRA, DPO, distillation and model editing for Mixtral, OLMoE and Qwen3-MoE with the same gradient bits on every machine: a fixed-order backward pass through the router and the experts, the load-balancing loss, LoRA adapters on the experts and ROME edits of the routed expert

title: Phase 44: Exact shared-expert mixtures
description: Mixtures of experts with a shared expert every token runs, gated by an exactly specified sigmoid or not: Qwen1.5/Qwen2-MoE from Hugging Face and GGUF and Granite MoE with its fused experts, on CPU and GPU, in the specification, the reference implementation, fine-tuning, LoRA and model editing

title: Phase 45: Reproducible quantised fine-tuning
description: LoRA fine-tuning on a Q8_0 or Q4_0 base with the same bits on every machine: the frozen weights stay quantised in memory and are defined exactly as their dequantised values, so runs, checkpoints, receipts, merged exports, DPO and distillation work as for float bases

title: Phase 46: Deterministic MCP elicitation and roots
description: The MCP host completed for interactive servers: servers that ask the client for structured input get exact, schema-valid answers from the engine, roots are offered in a fixed order, and the engine's sampling and elicitation answers are recorded in agent transcripts and checked offline by dllm replay

title: Phase 47: Exact SentencePiece models through GGUF
description: GGUF files with a SentencePiece vocabulary (TinyLlama, Llama 2, Mistral, Phi-3 quantisations) imported with a tokenizer that follows SentencePiece's own merge order exactly, verified against the sentencepiece library, and SentencePiece-style models exported back to GGUF, so these models round-trip through llama.cpp's format with the same bits

title: Phase 48: Tool calling in each model's own format
description: Tool calls in the format each model was trained on, detected from its own chat template: Hermes, Llama 3 JSON, Mistral [TOOL_CALLS] and Granite <|tool_call|>, constrained and parsed in that format with special marker tokens kept visible, and call ids each template accepts, with the same bits on every run

title: Phase 49: Exact modern samplers
description: DRY, XTC, locally typical and top-n-sigma sampling with exactly defined bits: llama.cpp's parameters in the OpenAI, completions and Ollama APIs and the CLI, recorded in receipts only when set, in the specification, the reference implementation, conformance vectors and dllm verify --reference

title: Phase 50: Exact adaptive samplers
description: Mirostat 1.0 and 2.0 and entropy-based dynamic temperature with exactly defined bits: the surprise target carried across tokens, the Zipf estimate and powers from the portable exp and log, in the OpenAI, completions and Ollama APIs and the CLI, the specification, the reference implementation, conformance vectors and dllm verify --reference

title: Phase 51: Exact complete GBNF grammars
description: GBNF grammars as complete as llama.cpp's and beyond, with exactly defined bits: left-recursive rules rewritten exactly, token references and their negations, lazy grammars that start at a trigger word, in the OpenAI and completions APIs, the CLI, receipts and the specification

title: Phase 52: Tool calling in more model formats
description: Tool calls in three more formats models are trained on, detected from their own chat template: Qwen3-Coder's XML parameters, DeepSeek's tool call markers and Python-style call lists, each constrained to the offered tools and their schemas and read back exactly, with the same bits on every run

title: Phase 53: Exact tool call controls
description: Tool calls controlled exactly: strict tools whose arguments are enforced by the full JSON Schema machinery in every tool format, parallel_tool_calls and disable_parallel_tool_use limiting an answer to one call, and allowed tools that narrow the callable set without changing the prompt, in every API, receipts and the response cache

title: Phase 54: Tool calling in the remaining formats
description: Tool calls in the formats left over from Phases 48 and 52, detected from each model's own chat template: Phi-4-mini's functools lists with the tools in the system message, DeepSeek V3.1's changed markers and Command R7B's action blocks, constrained to the offered tools and read back exactly, with the same bits on every run

title: Phase 55: Encoder embedding models
description: Small encoder embedding models (BERT, all-MiniLM, bge) imported from Hugging Face with exact WordPiece tokenizers, a new LayerNorm kernel with a documented order, bidirectional attention and CLS or mean pooling, in the specification and the reference implementation, so retrieval runs on purpose-built embedders with the same bits on every machine

title: Phase 56: Exact cross-encoder rerankers
description: BERT cross-encoders that score a query and a document together: exact sentence-pair encoding with token types, sequence-classification heads with an exactly specified pooler, and dllm rerank, /v1/rerank and hybrid search reranked by purpose-built rerankers, in the specification and the reference implementation, with the same scores on every machine

title: Phase 57: Unigram tokenizers and RoBERTa encoders
description: RoBERTa and XLM-RoBERTa encoders imported from Hugging Face with exact Unigram tokenizers (SentencePiece's precompiled normalizer, Metaspace and Viterbi segmentation with a total order), checked against the tokenizers library on every code point, so multilingual embedders and rerankers run with the same bits on every machine

title: Phase 58: Fine-tuning and exporting encoders
description: BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-RoBERTa encoders fine-tuned with exactly defined gradients (a LayerNorm backward kernel, bidirectional attention and the erf GELU), embedders trained contrastively on query and passage pairs and cross-encoders on labelled pairs, LoRA adapters for encoders, and encoders exported back to safetensors and GGUF, with byte-identical results on every machine
